content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Hypersonic Defense (program element 0604181C) is a Missile Defense Agency (MDA) research and development program funded through the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"3e6c34ae051f2791"}},{"text":"The program addresses defense against adversary hypersonic strike capabilities — hypersonics being weapons that travel at extremely high speeds and maneuver in ways that make them hard to intercept.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"According to the program's mission narrative, strategic competitors and adversaries are heavily investing in offensive and defensive hypersonic capabilities and currently have operational hypersonic strike and defensive systems deployed, which are challenges that U.S. Missile Defense policy, strategy, and capabilities must address.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"The program plans to develop a regional Glide Phase Interceptor capability to engage hypersonic threats during the glide phase of flight, with a Preliminary Design Review planned in FY 2028, a Kill Vehicle demonstration in 2029, and delivery of 12 tactical missiles in 2032.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"The program includes cooperatively developing the Glide Phase Interceptor with Japan.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"The Regional Hypersonic Missile Defense Capability effort uses the proven Aegis Weapon System as the point of departure, providing an additional layer of regional hypersonic defense from an Aegis ship, virtualized Aegis platform, or other fire control solution.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"The program element contains a project MD29, titled Hypersonic Defense.","citation":{"fact_id":"bc7598af5b9cd3a2"}},{"text":"It also contains a project MD40, titled Program Wide Support, which covers non-headquarters management costs supporting MDA functions across the entire Missile Defense System, allocated on a pro-rata basis across most Agency program elements.","citation":{"fact_id":"b9ada7a1b45fc768"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"The program's total funding rose from $182.283 million (shown as 182,283 in USD thousands) in fiscal year 2025 to $447.627 million (447,627 in USD thousands) in fiscal year 2026.","citation":{"fact_id":"25672186d678700d"}},{"text":"That represents an increase of about $265.344 million (265,344 in USD thousands), or roughly 146%, from FY2025 to FY2026 — a large single-year jump that signals expanded priority for the effort.","citation":{"fact_id":"8852af6b4a58cdba"}},{"text":"In fiscal year 2024 the program recorded actual spending of $228.962 million (228,962 in USD thousands), so the FY2026 total also exceeds the FY2024 level.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}},{"text":"The FY2026 total is composed of a $200.627 million (200,627 in USD thousands) discretionary request plus a $247 million (247,000 in USD thousands) reconciliation request.","citation":{"fact_id":"9810d0900b2d0e06"}},{"text":"The program submission reflects changes tied to the President's January 27, 2025 Executive Order, which established a goal of protecting U.S. citizens, safeguarding critical infrastructure, and securing second-strike capability against missile attack from any adversary.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf4b4504fe1fafe6"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The Missile Defense Agency (MDA) is the organization responsible for the Hypersonic Defense program.","citation":{"fact_id":"3e6c34ae051f2791"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings by Lockheed Martin Corporation referenced the FY2026 Department of Defense Appropriations Act (S 2572/HR 4016) including issues related to hypersonics.","citation":{"fact_id":"04eea92ddae3e4b9"}},{"text":"A 2026 lobbying filing by Lockheed Martin Corporation referenced space and missile defense issues in the FY2026 defense appropriations bill.","citation":{"fact_id":"002d7f7f516bc2f9"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings by Cerberus Capital Management, L.P. referenced issues pertaining to hypersonic technologies alongside the National Defense Authorization Act and defense appropriations.","citation":{"fact_id":"155431a38b1891be"}},{"text":"A 2025 lobbying filing by Cerberus Capital Management, L.P. referenced hypersonic technologies in the context of the FY2026 NDAA and Defense Appropriations.","citation":{"fact_id":"00e98daa090b2c4a"}},{"text":"A 2026 lobbying filing by Honeywell International Inc. referenced the Department of Defense Appropriations Act and NDAA with a hypersonic matched term.","citation":{"fact_id":"14bd8eb4652d11c2"}},{"text":"Venus Aerospace reported lobbying on issues related to hypersonic funding and programs in the House and Senate versions of the FY2024 Defense Appropriations Act.","citation":{"fact_id":"4073f942455b7a3c"}},{"text":"A 2025 lobbying filing by Venus Aerospace referenced hypersonic issues in the FY26 National Defense Authorization Act (H.R. 3038) and the FY26 Defense Appropriations Act.","citation":{"fact_id":"7299b133b8f77577"}},{"text":"Firehawk Aerospace reported lobbying on additive manufacturing for next-generation rocket propellant technologies in FY25 defense appropriations, with a hypersonic matched term.","citation":{"fact_id":"088325739d65503f"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
